B3a-05-mammalian-heart-internal-section

Longitudinal (vertical) section of the mammalian heart in front view (so the right side of the heart is on the viewer's left). Show the four chambers with the thin-walled atria at the top and thick-walled ventricles below, the left ventricle wall clearly thickest, the septum, the tricuspid and bicuspid valves with chordae tendineae and papillary muscles, semilunar valves at the base of the pulmonary artery and aorta, and the major vessels. Blood on the right side tinted blue and on the left side tinted red, with small arrows showing flow. The muscular wall of the left ventricle must be drawn clearly the thickest part of the heart, about three times thicker than the wall of the right ventricle and visibly thicker than the walls of the atria.
B3a-01-surface-area-volume-cubes

Three cubes of increasing size side by side (1 cm, 2 cm and 4 cm), drawn in 3D with the faces lightly shaded in soft blue, the smallest cube on the left. Under each cube, a small blank panel for its numbers. Beside them, a simple sketch of a tiny round Amoeba with short arrows showing oxygen diffusing in all round its surface, and a larger blob-shaped animal where arrows from the surface stop short of the deep centre cells.
B3a-06-human-heart-external-anatomy

External front view of the human heart showing its shape, the coronary arteries branching over the surface of the ventricles, and the great vessels at the top. Soft red and pink tones for the muscle, red for arteries and blue for veins.
B3a-07-cardiac-cycle-stages

Three-panel diagram of the cardiac cycle, each panel showing a simple section of the heart. Panel 1: whole heart relaxed, blood (blue on right, red on left) flowing into the atria and on into the ventricles, atrioventricular valves open, semilunar valves closed. Panel 2: atria contracting (drawn slightly smaller), arrows pushing blood into the ventricles. Panel 3: ventricles contracting, atrioventricular valves closed, semilunar valves open, arrows showing blood leaving through the pulmonary artery and aorta.
B3a-08-vein-valve-mechanism

Diagram of a valve in a vein shown in longitudinal section in two panels. Left panel: blood flowing towards the heart pushes the pocket valve open. Right panel: blood trying to flow backwards fills the pockets and closes the valve. Beside it, a leg vein between two contracting skeletal muscles with arrows showing the muscle squeezing blood upwards. Blue blood.
B3a-14-blood-clotting-cascade-flowchart

Flow diagram of blood clotting. Top: a cut in a small blood vessel with red blood cells and platelets escaping, and platelets sticking to the damaged edges. Middle: a simple arrow chain with boxes: damaged tissue and platelets release thromboplastin; prothrombin changes to thrombin (with calcium ions and vitamin K shown as small helper icons); fibrinogen changes to fibrin. Bottom: a close-up of a mesh of fibrin threads with red blood cells trapped in it, forming a clot.
B3a-15-blood-smear-cellular-composition

Blood smear as seen under a light microscope: many pale red biconcave red blood cells (some shown side-on to reveal the dumbbell profile), with one example of each white cell type stained purple: a neutrophil with a lobed nucleus, a lymphocyte with a large round nucleus, a monocyte with a kidney-shaped nucleus, an eosinophil with a two-lobed nucleus and pink granules, a basophil with dark granules, and a few small platelets.
B3a-16-human-lymphatic-system-anatomy

Outline of the human body in front view showing the lymphatic system in pale green: a network of lymph vessels throughout the arms, legs and trunk, clusters of bean-shaped lymph nodes in the neck, armpits and groin, the thoracic duct running up the middle of the chest and emptying into the left subclavian vein near the heart, the right lymphatic duct, and the spleen, thymus and tonsils. An inset box shows a close-up of a lymph node with lymph vessels entering and leaving and valves inside a lymph vessel.
B3a-09-capillary-bed-tissue-exchange

Capillary bed between an arteriole (left, red) and a venule (right, blue), with the capillary gradually changing from red to purple to blue along its length. Body cells surround it, bathed in pale yellow tissue fluid. Arrows show fluid leaving the capillary at the arterial end and most fluid re-entering at the venous end. A blind-ended lymph capillary (pale green) lies among the cells, collecting the extra fluid. Small labelled arrows show oxygen and glucose moving into the cells and carbon dioxide moving out.
B3a-10-blood-vessel-transverse-sections

Transverse sections of an artery, a vein and a capillary side by side, drawn to show relative wall thickness (not to scale for size). Artery: thick wall with outer connective tissue, thick middle layer of muscle and elastic fibres (pink and yellow), thin endothelium and small round lumen. Vein: thin wall with the same three layers, the middle layer thin, and a large irregular lumen. Capillary: a ring made of a single layer of flat cells with one red blood cell inside.
B3a-18-earthworm-closed-circulatory-system

Simplified side view of the front part of an earthworm showing its closed circulatory system: a dorsal blood vessel above the gut with forward-pointing arrows, a ventral blood vessel below the gut with backward-pointing arrows, five pairs of looping "hearts" joining them around the gut in the front segments, and fine capillary networks in the body wall of one segment. Blood vessels in red.
